Offer intravenous liothyronine (Triostat; myxedema coma) with disposition from hypothyroid patients (Steven L. Shafer, 2026-11-19). Nicoloff 1972 (J Clin Invest 51:473-483, PMC302152) gave IV 125I-T3 to 9 primary hypothyroid patients; the abstract gives only kT3 0.50 /day (half-life 1.38 days). Read the hypothyroid group's T3 distribution space (L) and clearance (L/day), its weights, ages and sexes, and the equilibration time (about 32 h, 10 h longer than normal) from the tables; check whether the curves support two compartments. Then add IV units (mcg, mcg/hr) to liothyronine as a route-limited parallel system (as meloxicam's IV fit is), absolute disposition (no F), anchored at Nicoloff's hypothyroid cohort; keep the oral Van Tassell steady-state model. Van Tassell's hypothyroid first-dose fit (12-h sampling, half-life 3.6 h, implied CL 86 L/day) is not to be used: it is the distribution phase.
